title: Emergency Production Change With a Security-Incident Qualifier
scenario_text:
You are the on-call release manager at Rutherford Media. A senior engineer wants to push a change to the production payment service right now, outside the normal change window, to patch an actively exploited authentication-bypass vulnerability. It is 2:00 AM Saturday.

Active policy: Change Management Policy CM-4, effective 2024-06-01. Standard production changes require a Change Advisory Board (CAB) ticket approved 24 hours in advance. Two expedited paths exist: (1) Expedited change — a Director may approve a same-day change with reduced review for routine urgent fixes; (2) Emergency Security change — when a change remediates an active security incident (a confirmed, exploited vulnerability logged in the incident tracker), it may be deployed immediately with a single on-call Security Officer approval, and the CAB is reviewed retrospectively within 48 hours.

Precedent (change log): 2024-07-19, off-window hotfix to the checkout service, approved by Engineering Director Omar Reyes via the Expedited path. Note: "Latency regression causing cart abandonment — urgent but not a security incident. Director-approved expedited change."

Current facts: Security has logged incident INC-4471, confirming the auth-bypass is being actively exploited against the payment service. A Security Officer, Dana Kohl, is on call and reachable. The engineer says, "Last time we did an off-window fix, Omar just approved it as an expedited change — let's get a Director to do the same and move fast."
question: Which approval path should authorize this off-window production change? Give the path name and the single approver role required to deploy immediately.
